steps.label: Pull 6-12 months
steps.sub: real request rate, CPU/memory, storage history

steps.label: Fit the right model
steps.sub: linear vs. compounding — plot it first

steps.label: Add a confidence band
steps.sub: plan to the upper bound, not the midpoint

code:
month_over_month_delta = [120, 118, 125, 121, 119]   # roughly constant
#  -> LINEAR growth: plan with simple trend + slope

month_over_month_pct   = [8%, 9%, 8%, 10%, 9%]       # roughly constant %
#  -> COMPOUNDING growth: absolute increment is still growing
#     a linear fit here will undercount the further out you look
caption: Plot the real history first — constant absolute delta vs. constant percent delta tells you which model to fit.

code:
forecast_midpoint_rps   = 40000   # 'most likely' peak next quarter
forecast_upper_bound_rps = 52000  # upper edge of the confidence band
headroom_buffer         = 1.25    # +25% margin above the upper bound

capacity_target_rps = forecast_upper_bound_rps * headroom_buffer
# = 65000 rps  <- this is the number that drives procurement,
#                 not the 40000 'average' estimate
caption: The number that drives a scaling decision is the upper bound plus headroom — never the midpoint.

subtitle: Turning a capacity number into a test that proves the system can actually handle it.
